No loads found in the model external XML file for the given service point.
The load customer count may be modified from its original value.
The transformer-bank ID is same as another transformer ID in this substation.
Message.Explanation: Transformer and transformer-bank have the same ID.

Message.MessageText: A model was not assigned as the model was not found in the global file or the global_internals.xml file.
Message.Explanation: An associated model for the device was not assigned.
Message.Solution: Assign a model to the device and define the model in the global.csv file or the global_internals.xml file.

Message.MessageText: A valid Id was not given. No more validation for this device can occur.
The total load is greater than the transformer nominal rating.
Message.Explanation: The total connected load is greater than the transformer loading (%) of power flow options frame in the converter options tab of the total transformer kVA rating.
Message.Solution: Check the Load.PNomA, PNomB, PNomC XML fields or the PNOMA_LOAD, PNOMB_LOAD, PNOMC_LOAD CSV fields and the associated transformer model's SRating XML field or SRATING_TFMOD CSV field. Make sure the sum of all three phases' nominal load are not greater than the transformer loading (%) of power flow options frame in the converter options tab of total transformer kVA rating.

Message.MessageText: The load phase does not exist at the connection node.
Message.Explanation: Load has a phase that is not present on the line/device that feeds the load.
Message.Solution: This typically happens when a load is delta connected but is fed by a single phase line. If so, check the winding type on the load.

Message.MessageText: The nominal real power is not close to the average real power over all phases.
Message.Explanation: The difference in the total load of one phase and the average load over all phases is greater than the user-specified loading imbalance value specified in the Power Flow Options frame in the Converter Options tab.
Message.Solution: Check the Load.PNomA, PNomB, PNomC, Phase XML fields or the PNOMA_LOAD, PNOMB_LOAD, PNOMC_LOAD, PHASE_LOAD CSV fields, and/or change the load values or the loading imbalance value specified in the Power Flow Options frame in the Converter Options tab to a more reasonable value.

Message.MessageText: The real power is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The nominal real power (kW) over one phase is outside its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the Load.PNomA, PNomB, PNomC XML fields or the PNOMA_LOAD, PNOMB_LOAD, PNOMC_LOAD CSV fields, and change the nominal real power (kW) over one phase to a value inside the acceptable range. Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The reactive power is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The nominal reactive power (kVAR) over one phase is outside its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the Load.QNomA, QNomB, QNomC XML fields or the QNOMA_LOAD, QNOMB_LOAD, QNOMC_LOAD CSV fields, and change the nominal reactive power (kVAR) over one phase to a value inside the acceptable range. Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The number of customers represented by this load is outside of the acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The number of customers represented by this load is outside the acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the Load.Customer XML field or the CUSTOMER_LOAD CSV field, and change the number of customers to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The shunt impedance phase does not exist at the connection node.
Message.Explanation: Capacitor has a phase that is not present on the line/device that connects to the capacitor.

Message.MessageText: The ON level is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The on level value is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Change the shunt impedance capacitor's OnLevel XML field or ONLEVEL_SHIMP CSV field to a value inside the acceptable range. Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The OFF level is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The off level value is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Change the shunt impedance capacitor's OffLevel XML field or OFFLEVEL_SHIMP CSV field to a value inside the acceptable range. Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The reactive power is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The nominal reactive power injection (kVAR) over one phase is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the shunt impedance capacitor's Qtotal XML field or QTOTAL_SHIMP field, and change the nominal reactive power (kVAR) over one phase to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The can size is greater than the total kVAR of the installation.
Message.Explanation: The size of the individual units that make up the bank is greater than the total kVAR over all three phases.
Message.Solution: Check the shunt impedance capacitor's CellSize and Qtotal XML fields, or CELLSIZE_SHIMP and QTOTAL_SHIMP CSV fields, and change the size of cell or total KVAR over all three phases to a correct value.

Message.MessageText: The nominal voltage is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The line to neutral nominal voltage is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the NomKV, VoltEnum, Volt_Units XML fields or the NOMKV_* CSV field, and change the nominal voltage to a value inside the acceptable range.

Message.MessageText: The number of controller steps is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The number of steps for the controller is outside of its acceptable ranges.
Message.Solution: Check the shunt impedance capacitor's NumSteps XML field or the NUMSTEPS_SHIMP CSV field, and change the number of steps to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The step size is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The step size (kVAR) is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the shunt impedance capacitor's StepSize and Qtotal XML fields, or the STEPSIZE_SHIMP and QTOTAL_SHIMP CSV fields, and change the step size to a value inside the acceptable range (1~total nominal KVAR over all three phases).

Message.MessageText: The daily maximum number of switchings is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The daily maximum number of switching operations is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the shunt impedance capacitor's MaxSwitches XML field or the MAXSWITCHES_SHIMP CSV field, and change the daily maximum number of switching operations to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The time between consecutive switching operations is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The time between consecutive switching operations (hours) is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the shunt impedance capacitor's Consecsw XML field or the CONSECSW_SHIMP CSV field, and change time between consecutive switching operations to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The time delay is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The controller time delay setting (seconds) is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the shunt impedance capacitor's Tdelay XML field and the TDELAY_SHIMP CSV field, or the composite switch's TimeDelay XML field and TIMEDELAY_COMPSW CSV field, or the Fault Detector TimeDelay XML field and TIMEDELAY_FDTECT CSV field, and change the time delay setting to a value inside the acceptable range. Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The nominal voltage is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The nominal voltage(kV) is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the Series Reactor's NomKV XML field or NOMKV_SERIES CSV field, and change the nominal voltage to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The total connected load is less than the given threshold of the transformer rating.
Message.Explanation: The total connected load is less than the given threshold of the total transformer kVA rating.
Message.Solution: Check the associated transformer model's SRating XML field or SRATING_TFMOD CSV field for the transformer, PNomA, PNomB, PNomC CSV fields, or PNOMA_LOAD, PNOMB_LOAD, PNOMC_LOAD CSV fields of all connected load, load scaling factor of power flow options frame in converter options tab. Make sure the sum of all three phases' nominal loads are not less than given threshold of total transformer kVA rating.

Message.MessageText: The single-phase transformer rating is too high.
The primary voltage is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The primary nominal voltage (kV), that is measured line to ground, is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the transformer's PrimVolt XML field or PRIMVOLT_TF CSV field, and change the primary nominal voltage to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The secondary voltage is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The secondary nominal voltage (kV), that is measured line to ground, is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the transformer's SecVolt XML field or SECVOLT_TF CSV field, and change the secondary nominal voltage to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The tertiary voltage is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The tertiary nominal voltage (kV), that is measured line to ground, is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the transformer's TertVolt XML field or TERTVOLT_TF CSV field, and change tertiary nominal voltage to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The customer count is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The number of connected customers is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the transformer's Customer XML field or CUSTOMER_TF CSV field, and change the number of connected customers to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: A three winding transformer must be assigned to a transformer model that supports three winding transformers.
Message.Explanation: A non-connection of tertiary winding for the three winding transformer exists.
Message.Solution: Check the associated transformer model's TfType field or transformer's CnsType field, and change the connection type of tertiary winding for associated transformer model for the transformer to not be a non-connection. Connection definition for transformer power flow types is represented in the Modeling Reference Tables spreadsheet.

Message.MessageText: The maximum separation voltage is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The maximum separation voltage (p.u. or volt) is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the generator's VmaxSep XML field or VMAXSEP_GEN CSV field, and change the maximum separation voltage to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The minimum separation voltage is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The minimum separation voltage (p.u. or volt) is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the generator's VminSep XML field or VMINSEP_GEN CSV field, and change the minimum separation voltage to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The minimum separation voltage is greater than the maximum separation voltage.
Message.Explanation: The minimum separation voltage is greater than the maximum separation voltage.
Message.Solution: Check the generator's VmaxSep and VminSep XML fields, or VMAXSEP_GEN and VMINSEP_GEN CSV fields, and make sure the maximum separation voltage is not less than minimum separation voltage.

Message.MessageText: The node associated with the inverter does not have a DER device attached.
Message.Explanation: The node associated with the inverter does not have a DER device attached.
Message.Solution: Ensure that the node is set correctly for the inverter, and that a DER device is also connected to the node.

Message.MessageText: The inverter does not have a valid node associated.
Message.Explanation: The inverter does not have a valid node associated.
Message.Solution: Ensure that a valid node is associated with the inverter.

Message.MessageText: The phase configured for the Inverter and its DER does not match.
Message.Explanation: The phase configured for the Inverter and its DER does not match.
Message.Solution: Ensure that the phases of the Inverter and its DER match.

Message.MessageText: The inverter real power limits are not consistent with the associated DER device limits.
The inverter reactive power limits are not consistent with the associated DER device limits.
The associated transformer for the tap changer could not be found.
The PT secondary voltage is outside of its acceptable range.
The associated tap changer model for a tap could not be found.
Message.Explanation: The associated tap changer model for a tap could not be found.
Message.Solution: Check the transformer's PrTapModel, ScTapModel, and TeTapModel XML fields, or PRTAPMODEL_TF, SCTAPMODEL_TF, and TETAPMODEL_TF CSV fields. Assign a model to the tap changer and model must be defined in the global.csv or global_internals.xml file.

Message.MessageText: The CT secondary amp value is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The CT full secondary amps rating value is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the transformer's PrCTFullAmps, ScCTFullAmps, TeCTFullAmps, PrCtSecamps, ScCtSecamps, and TeCtSecamps XML fields, or PRCTFULLAMPS_DEFTF, SCCTFULLAMPS_DEFTF, TECTFULLAMPS_DEFTF, PRCTSECAMPS_TF, SCCTSECAMPS_TF, and TECTSECAMPS_TF CSV fields, and change CT full secondary amps value to a value inside the acceptable range.

Message.MessageText: The line drop compensation resistance is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The line drop compensation resistance is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the transformer's PrLdcR, ScLdcR, and TeLdcR XML fields or PRLDCR_TF, SCLDCR_TF, and TELDCR_TF CSV fields, and change the line drop compensation resistance to a value inside the acceptable range (0 - 100 ohms).

Message.MessageText: The line drop compensation reactance is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The line drop compensation reactance is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the transformer's PrLdcX, ScLdcX, and TeLdcX XML fields or PRLDCX_TF, SCLDCX_TF, and TELDCX_TF CSV fields, and change the line drop compensation reactance to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The value given for the PT ratio is suspect.
Message.Explanation: The PT ratio calculated voltage is not close to the voltage on the regulation side.
Message.Solution: Check the transformer's PrPtRatio, ScPtRatio, TePtRatio, PrVtarget, ScVtarget, TeVtarget, PrimVolt, SecVolt, and TertVolt XML fields or PRPTRATIO_TF, SCPTRATIO_TF, TEPTRATIO_TF, PRVTARGET_TF, SCVTARGET_TF, TEVTARGET_TF, PRIMVOLT_TF, SECVOLT_TF, and TERTVOLT_TF CSV fields. Change line to ground voltage calculated from the PT ratio and target voltage to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The CT ratio is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The CT ratio for a tap changer is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the transformer's PrCtRatio, ScCtRatio, and TeCtRatio XML fields or PRCTRATIO_TF, SCCTRATIO_TF, and TECTRATIO_TF CSV fields, and change CT ratio over one winding to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The PT ratio is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The PT ratio for a tap changer is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the transformer's PrPtRatio, ScPtRatio, and TePtRatio XML fields or PRPTRATIO_TF, SCPTRATIO_TF, and TEPTRATIO_TF CSV fields, and change PT ratio over one winding to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The regulation node has not been correctly set.
Message.Explanation: The regulation node for a tap changer has not been set.
Message.Solution: Check the transformer's FromNode, ToNode, and TertiaryNode XML fields or FRNODE_TF, TONODE_TF, and TENODE_TF CSV fields and regulation node type XML fields PrimaryRegNode, SecondaryRegNode, TertiaryRegNode. Change the regulation node value to correct value according to the regulation node type.

Message.MessageText: The tap changer model has not been correctly set.
Message.Explanation: The tap changer model has not been set for tap changer.
Message.Solution: Check the transformer's PrTapModel, ScTapModel, TeTapModel XML fields or PRTAPMODEL_TF, SCTAPMODEL_TF, TETAPMODEL_TF CSV fields. Assign a model to the tap changer and define the model in the global.csv file or global_internals.xml.

Message.MessageText: The tap changer has not been properly assigned to the transformer.
Message.Explanation: The tap changer's associated transformer has not been found.
Message.Solution: Need to check whether the transformer has been set to the tap changer successfully by code.

Message.MessageText: The voltage target setting is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The voltage target setting is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the transformer's PrVtarget, ScVtarget, TeVtarget XML fields or PRVTARGET_TF, SCVTARGET_TF, TEVTARGET_TF CSV fields, and change the voltage target setting for the tap changer's associated transformer to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The bandwidth is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The voltage bandwidth for the tap changer is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the transformer's PrBandwth, ScBandwth, TeBandwth XML fields or PRBANDWTH_TF, SCBANDWTH_TF, TEBANDWTH_TF CSV fields, and change the voltage bandwidth setting for the tap changer's associated transformer to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The voltage setpoint range is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The voltage setpoint voltage range for the tap changer is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the transformer's PrVoltSetpointRangeMin, PrVoltSetpointRangeMax, ScVoltSetpointRangeMin, ScVoltSetpointRangeMax, TeVoltSetpointRangeMin, TeVoltSetpointRangeMax in XML fields, and change the voltage minimum or maximum voltage setpoint range setting for the tap changer's associated transformer to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The normal tap setting is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The normal tap setting is outside of its acceptable range given on the tap model.
Message.Solution: Check the transformer's PrNormTap, ScNormTap, TeNormTap XML fields or PRNORMTAP_TF, SCNORMTAP_TF,TENORMTAP_TF CSV fields, and the associated tap model's MaxTap and MinTap XML fields or MAXTAP_TAPMOD and MINTAP_TAPMOD CSV fields, and change the normal tap setting to a value inside the acceptable range (min tap - max tap of associated tap model).

Message.MessageText: The default feeder color is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The default feeder color is outside of its acceptable range.

Message.Solution: Check all feeders in the substation's DefColor XML fields or DEFCOLOR_FEEDER CSV field, and make sure the color of every feeder is unique.

Message.MessageText: The grounding reactance is outside of its acceptable range.

Message.MessageText: The nominal voltage is outside of its acceptable range.
The length is outside of its acceptable range.

Message.Solution: Check the line's Length XML field or LENGTH_LINE CSV field, and change the line length to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The number of circuits in a duct bank is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The number of circuits in a duct bank is outside of its acceptable range.

Message.MessageText: The default override temporary failure rate is outside of its acceptable range.
The default override permanent failure rate is outside of its acceptable range.
The default override repair time is outside of its acceptable range.
The line length is less than the allowable minimum - length will be changed to the minimum value.
The load has zero customers.
Message.Explanation: The load has zero customers associated with it.
Message.Solution: Check the Load's Customer XML field or CUSTOMER_LOAD CSV field, and change the number of customers associated with the load to a positive number.

Message.MessageText: There are multiple station boundary switches for this composite switch.
Message.Explanation: This composite switch has multiple boundary switches.
Message.Solution: Check the switch's ToStation XML field or TOSUB_SWITCH CSV field, and make sure that the boundary switch number in this composite switch is not greater than 1.

Message.MessageText: A valid nominal state does not exist for this composite switch. Check the global composite switch model.
Message.Explanation: The nominal state for this composite switch does not exist in the state list of associated composite switch model.
Message.Solution: Check the switch's NormOpenPhases XML field or NORM_OPEN_PHASES CSV field and associated composite switch model's NumStates and States XML fields or NUMSTATE_COMPSWMOD, STATENAMEn_COMPSWMOD, STATEn_COMPSWMOD CSV fields, and change the normally open phase value of switches in this composite switch so that the nominal state of the composite switch exists in the state list of associated composite switch models. The nominal state of composite switch is an integer equal to the base 10 equivalent of the combined binary states of the individual switch states. For example, a two-device switch that has both devices closed (represented in binary by 11) would have a nominal state value of 3.

Message.MessageText: The number of phase trip operations is outside of its acceptable range.

Message.MessageText: The number of phase trip operations is outside of its acceptable range.

Message.MessageText: There is no load connected to this transformer.
Message.Explanation: There is no load connected to lower voltage node of transformer.
Message.Solution: Check the transformer's ToNode and FromNode XML field or TONODE_TF, FRNODE_TF CSV fields, and make sure the lower voltage node of the transformer has load.

Message.MessageText: The transformer collection for the transformer bank was incorrectly set.
Message.Explanation: The first transformer for the transformer bank was incorrectly set.

Message.MessageText: Error in processing transformers for the transformer bank.

Message.Solution: Need to check whether the transformer of the transformer bank has been set successfully by code.

Message.MessageText: Different transformer types are assigned to transformers in a transformer bank.
Message.Explanation: A transformer type that is different from one of the first transformer has been assigned to other transformers in a transformer bank.
Message.Solution: Check the associated transformer model's TfType XML field or TFTYPE_TFMOD CSV field, transformer's CnsType field or CNSTTYPE_TF CSV field, and make sure the same transformer type is assigned to each transformer in the transformer bank.

Message.MessageText: Two transformers with the same phase exist for a transformer bank.
Message.Explanation: Other transformer has the same phase as the first transformer for a transformer bank.
Message.Solution: Check the transformer's Phase or PrimPhase XML field, PRIMPHASE_TF CSV field, and make sure no transformer has the same phase as the first transformer.

Message.MessageText: The setting group ScadaIndex Value is outside of its acceptable range.

Message.Solution: Check the construction model's Voltage XML field, VOLTAGE_CNSTMOD CSV field or voltage level's ValuekV XML field, VALUEKV_VOLTLEVEL, and change the construction voltage to a value inside the acceptable range (1 - 500) or change the user line to line voltage level value to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The X spatial coordinate is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The construction X spatial coordinate is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the construction model's XaCoord, XbCoord, XcCoord, XnCoord XML fields or XACOORD_CNSTMOD, XBCOORD_CNSTMOD, XCCOORD_CNSTMOD, XNCOORD_CNSTMOD CSV fields, and change the X spatial coordinate to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The Y spatial coordinate is outside of its acceptable range.

Message.MessageText: The shield thickness is outside of its acceptable range for a tape shielded cable.

Message.MessageText: The permanent fault rate is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The sustained failure rate is outside of its acceptable range.

Message.MessageText: A value of uninterrupted service is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: A value of uninterrupted service is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the load category's PCostInt, ECostInt XML fields or PCOSTINT_LOADCAT, ECOSTINT_LOADCAT CSV fields, and change the value of uninterrupted service to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: A load allocation accuracy of 40.0% was assigned.
Message.Explanation: A load allocation accuracy is 0, 40% will be assigned.

Message.MessageText: The load schedule data accuracy is outside of its acceptable range.

Message.MessageText: The normal voltage limit should be within the range of emergency voltage limit.
Message.Explanation: The emergency high voltage limit should be greater than normal voltage high limit, while emergency low voltage limit should be less than normal low voltage limit.

Message.MessageText: The voltage limit cost is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The voltage limit violation cost is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the load category's VLimitCost XML field or VLIMCOST_LOADCAT CSV field, and change the voltage limit violation cost to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The voltage imbalance cost is outside of its acceptable range.

Message.Solution: Check the load category's Vimbalance XML field or VIMBALANCE_LOADCAT CSV field, and change the voltage imbalance factor for three-phase loads to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: A load schedule type does not match for the load category (average vs. peak).
Message.Explanation: The peak load flag of a load schedule that is a flag indicating the load P and Q nominal values represent peak values does not match for the flag of load category.

Message.Solution: Check the schedule point's XValue XML field or XVALUE_SCHEDPT CSV field, and change the X axis value to a value inside the acceptable range. Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The first Y value for the schedule point is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The first Y value for the schedule point is outside of its acceptable range.

Message.MessageText: The second Y value for the schedule point is outside of its acceptable range.

Message.MessageText: The normal low limit is greater than the normal high limit.

Message.MessageText: There is an inconsistency among the (1) transformer rating (kVA or MVA) (2) excitation current (%) and (3) magnetizing loss (W).
Message.Explanation: The product of transformer rating (kVA or MVA) and excitation current (%) is less than magnetizing loss (W) for a transformer model when excitation current is greater than 0.
Message.Solution: Check the transformer model's SRating, ExciteCurrent, CoreLoss XML fields or SRATING_TFMOD, EXCITECURRENT_TFMOD, CORELOSS_TFMOD CSV fields, and make sure that the square of the product of transformer rating and excitation current is not less than the square of magnetizing loss. Message.Solution: Check the X0 XML field of conductor model and generator model or the X0_GENMOD, X0_CONDMOD CSV fields, and change the zero sequence reactance to the correct value. For a conductor model, the value should be greater than 0 ohm/kft. For a generator model, the value is in the range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.Explanation: The generator rating is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the generator model's KVA XML field or KVA_GENMOD CSV field, and change the generator rating to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.Explanation: The generator minimum reactive power output is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the generator model's QgenMin XML field or QGENMIN_GENMOD CSV field, and change the minimum reactive power output to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The generator operational cost is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The operational cost of switching on/off a generator is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the generator model's SwitchCost XML field or SWITCOST_GENMOD CSV field, and change the operational cost to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The capacitive rating is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The capacitive rating for a SVC model is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the SVC model's Caprating field, and change the capacitive rating to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The inductive rating is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The inductive rating for a SVC model is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the SVC model's Indrating field, and change the inductive rating to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The rated power factor for a generator/energy resource model is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The rated power factor for a generator/energy resource model is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the generator model's RATEDPF_GENMOD field or energy resource model's RATEDPF_ENERGYRESMOD, and change the rated power factor to a value between -1 and 1.

Message.MessageText: A regulation branch was not specified for the capacitor(the regulation branch type may also be incorrect).
Message.Explanation: A regulation branch was not specified for the capacitor.
Message.Solution: Check the shunt impedance capacitor's RegBranch XML field or REGBRANCH_SHIMP CSV field, and make sure that regulation branch ID is a valid line, switch, fuse, recloser, sectionalizer, network protector, transformer, breaker or jumper ID.

Message.MessageText: Both magnetizing loss and magnetizing power factor should be set if excitation current percentage is unset.
Incorrect parallel transformer was found.
Message.Explanation: The from or to node of transformers in a bank do not match; they are not in a parallel configuration for a transformer bank. Two transformers have the same to node when they are in different transformer banks, or one transformer is banked and another is not banked.
Message.Solution: Check all of the transformer's FromNode and ToNode fields or FRNODE_TF, TONODE_TF CSV fields, and make sure that all transformers in a bank have the same from and to nodes. Make sure that two transformers have different to nodes when they are in different transformer banks, or one transformer is banked and another is not banked.

Message.MessageText: Study load time bins do not cover each hour of the day.
Message.Explanation: The study load time interval bins do not cover each hour of the entire day for load category.
Message.Solution: Check the load category's DailyStudyInt.TimePeriods.StartTime and EndTime XML fields or STARTTIMEn_LOADCAT, ENDTIMEn_LOADCAT CSV fields, and make sure all study mode time interval bins can cover 0 - 23 hours.

Message.MessageText: The regulation node for the tap changer is not on downstream side of regulator. Regulator downstream node is used instead.
Message.Explanation: The regulation node for the tap changer is not on downstream side of regulator. Regulator downstream node is used instead.
Message.Solution: Check the transformer's FromNode, ToNode, TertiaryNode, PrimaryRegNode, SecondaryRegNode, TertiaryRegNode XML fields or FRNODE_TF, TONODE_TF, TENODE_TF CSV fields, and change the regulation node for the tap changer to the load node of the transformer.

Message.MessageText: The throwover switch is not in a valid state (in manual mode).
Message.Explanation: The throwover switch has two closed or opened switches when the associated composite switch model is in manual mode.
Message.Solution: Check the associated composite switch model's SwitchType XML field or SWITCHTYPE_COMPSWMOD CSV field, NormOpenPhases XML field or NORM_OPEN_PHASES CSV field for switches in the composite switch, and make sure that the number of normally opened or closed throwover switches is not 2.

Message.MessageText: The throwover switch is not in a valid state (in automatic mode).
Message.Explanation: The throwover switch has two closed or opened switches when the associated composite switch model is in automatic mode.
Message.Solution: Check the associated composite switch model's SwitchType XML field or SWITCHTYPE_COMPSWMOD CSV field, NormOpenPhases XML field or NORM_OPEN_PHASES CSV field for switches in the composite switch, and make sure that the number of normally opened or closed throwover switches is not 2.

Message.MessageText: An invalid voltage level color was given (a default value will be applied).
Message.Explanation: An invalid voltage level color was given in global data.
Message.Solution: Check the voltage level's Color XML field or COLOR_VOLTLEVEL CSV field, and change the voltage level color to a value inside the acceptable range.Please see e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: A duplicate voltage level color was found.
Message.Explanation: A duplicate voltage level color was found in a different voltage level.
Message.Solution: Check the voltage level's Color XML field or COLOR_VOLTLEVEL CSV field, and make sure that all voltage levels use a different color.

Message.MessageText: Regulation node is not connected to other devices (node is floating).
Message.Explanation: Regulation node for a tap changer is not connected to any downstream devices.
Message.Solution: Check the transformer's FromNode, ToNode, TertiaryNode, PrimaryRegNode, SecondaryRegNode, and TertiaryRegNode fields or FRNODE_TF, TONODE_TF, and TENODE_TF CSV fields, and make sure the regulation node has been connected to another downstream transformer device.

Message.MessageText: The device co-ordinates are outside the Converter bounding box co-ordinates.
Message.Explanation: The device coordinates are outside of the bounding box coordinates in the converter configuration.
Message.Solution: Check the placement's X and Y fields or WCX_*, WCY_*, LABELX_*, LABELY_* CSV fields, and change the device coordinates to be inside the bounding box coordinates.

Message.MessageText: The station has more than one slack generator.
Message.Explanation: The station has more than one slack generator.
Message.Solution: Check the generator's SlackGen XML field or SLACK_GEN CSV fields. The slackgen field is a flag indicating that a generator is a slack source (true = slack, false = not the slack source). Please make sure there are more than one electric islands in the substation if the number of slack generator is greater than 1.

Message.MessageText: The phase conductor diameter must be less than twice the value of the phase to neutral conductor spacing.
Message.Explanation: The phase conductor diameter must be less than twice the value of the phase to neutral conductor spacing for concentric neutral cable.
Message.Solution: Check the conductor model's Diameter and NeutDist XML fields or DIAMETER_CONDMOD, NEUTDIST_CONDMOD CSV fields, and make sure that the conductor model diameter is less than twice the value of the phase to neutral conductor spacing.

Message.MessageText: The diameter of the phase conductor must be larger than the diameter of a single neutral strand.
Message.Explanation: The diameter of the phase conductor must be larger than the diameter of a single neutral strand.
Message.Solution: Check the conductor model's Diameter and Diamneutral XML fields or DIAMETER_CONDMOD, DIAMNEUTRAL_CONDMOD CSV fields, and make sure that the conductor model diameter is greater than the diameter of a single neutral strand.

Message.MessageText: The tap changer measurement is assigned to fixed tap changer.
Message.Explanation: The tap changer measurement is assigned to a non-voltage regulation tap changer when tap changer position measurement is on the transformer primary side or secondary side.
Message.Solution: Check the status and analog's Terminal XML field or TERMINAL_STAT, TERMINAL_ANA CSV fields and transformer's Pcontrol, Scontrol, PrControllable, ScControllable, PriTap, SecTap fields or PRCONTROLABLE_TF, SCCONTROLABLE_TF CSV fields, and make sure that the tap changer measurement is assigned to the voltage regulation tap changer.

Message.MessageText: The tap changer mode is inconsistent with its control type.
Message.Explanation: The tap changer mode is inconsistent with its control type.
Message.Solution: Check the transformer's Pcontrol, Scontrol, TControl, PrControllable, ScControllable, TeControllable, PriTap, SecTap, TerTap fields or PRCONTROLABLE_TF, SCCONTROLABLE_TF CSV fields, and make sure that the tap changer is consistent with its control type. If tap is no tap or fixed tap, control mode should be not controllable. If tap is regulating tap, control mode should be controllable.

Message.MessageText: The transformer type value is outside the acceptable range
The critical customer number is greater than customer number on load
Message.Solution: Make sure the critical customer number is less than customer number

Message.MessageText: The critical flag on transformer is false but the number of critical customers is greater than 0
Message.Solution: Set the critical flag on Transformer True

Message.MessageText: Measurement type is not set
Message.Explanation: Measurement type cannot be null or 0
Message.Solution: Verify the measurement type and set the corresponding value

Message.MessageText: The regular load has negative scheduled real or reactive power
Message.Solution: Make sure the regular load does not have negative scheduled real or reactive power

Message.MessageText: The tap changer measurement is assigned to a nonexistent tap changer.
Message.Explanation: The tap changer measurement is on source side while transformer/regulator has no primary tap, or The tap changer measurement is on load side while trasformer/regulator has no secondary tap.
Message.Solution: Check the status and analog's Terminal XML field or TERMINAL_STAT, TERMINAL_ANA CSV fields and transformer's Pcontrol, Scontrol, PrControllable, ScControllable, PriTap, SecTap fields or PRCONTROLABLE_TF, SCCONTROLABLE_TF CSV fields, and make sure that the tap changer measurement is assigned to the correct tap changer.

Message.MessageText: The interface voltage range defined is not within the acceptable limits (0-10%).
Message.Solution: Make sure that the interface voltage range is within acceptable limits of (0-10%).

Message.MessageText: The transformer has more than one voltage regulating tap changer.
Message.Explanation: A transformer can have only one voltage regulating tap changer.
Message.Solution: One or more tap changers need to be changed to a fixed tap changer or the transformer must be modeled using multiple two-winding transformers.

Message.MessageText: The transformer critical customer flag is not consistent with the connected load critical customer count.
Message.Explanation: The critical flag on the transformer is true but the critical customer number is 0.
Message.Solution: Confirm that the transformer critical customer flag is set correctly and the critical customer count on the load(s) connected to this transformer is set correctly.

Message.MessageText: There is an unexpected number of status measurements associated with a ganged device.
Message.Explanation: There is an unexpected number of status measurements associated with a ganged device.
Message.Solution: Check the status measurement mapping for the device and verify that the correct status measurements have been assigned.

Message.MessageText: There is an unexpected number of control measurements associated with a ganged device.
Message.Explanation: There is an unexpected number of control measurements associated with a ganged device.
Message.Solution: Check the control measurement mapping for the device and verify that the correct control measurements have been assigned.

Message.MessageText: There is an unexpected number of status measurements associated with a phase independently operated device.
Message.Explanation: There is an unexpected number of status measurements associated with a phase independently operated device.
Message.Solution: Check the status measurement mapping for the device and verify that the correct status measurements have been assigned.

Message.MessageText: There is an unexpected number of control measurements associated with a phase independently operated device.
Message.Explanation: There is an unexpected number of control measurements associated with a phase independently operated device.
Message.Solution: Check the control measurement mapping for the device and verify that the correct control measurements have been assigned.

Message.MessageText: The given value is out of range.
Message.Explanation: The given value is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Change the given value to a value inside the acceptable range.

Message.MessageText: The number of customers with generation is larger than the total number of load customers.
Message.Explanation: The number of customers with generation is larger than the total number of load customers. The load customer counts need to be checked.
Message.Solution: Change the customer count numbers to their proper values.

Message.MessageText: Only one field is required. Either delete the MAGPF_TFMOD or EXCITECURENT_TFMOD.
Incorrect Nominal Load information
Device id for a feed does not exist.
Message.Explanation: The device id associated with one of the feeds for the reserved capacity object is non-existent.
Message.Solution: The field <FeedDeviceId> must be populated with a valid device id.

Message.MessageText: The specified units is incorrect.
Message.Explanation: The specified units for the reserved capacities is incorrect.
Message.Solution: The units should be 1 or 2 indicating kW or kVA respectively

Message.MessageText: Number of feeds outside range.
Message.Explanation: The number of feeds associated with the reserved capacity object is outside the acceptable range.

Message.MessageText: Number of load ids outside range.
Message.Explanation: The number of load ids associated with the reserved capacity object is outside the acceptable range.

Message.MessageText: Feed station reserved capacity is outside range.
Feed line reserved capacity is outside range.
Feed power factor out of range.
Message.Solution: The feed power factor must be between 0 and 1

Message.MessageText: The positive sequence resistance is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The positive sequence resistance is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the conductor model's R1 XML field or R1_CONDMOD CSV field, and change the positive sequence resistance to a value inside the acceptable range. Please see the e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The zero sequence resistance is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The zero sequence resistance is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the conductor model's R0 XML field or R0_CONDMOD CSV field, and change the zero sequence resistance to a value inside the acceptable range. Please see the e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: The positive sequence reactance is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: The positive sequence reactance is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Solution: Check the conductor model's X1 XML field or X1_CONDMOD CSV field, and change the positive sequence reactance to a value inside the acceptable range. Please see the e-terradistribution_modeling_reference_tables.xlsx for details.

Message.MessageText: Nodal voltage is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation:
Low load voltage could be due to several issues with the primary network model including excessive conductor and inline transformer voltage drops, incorrect regulator settings, incorrect distribution transformer size or impedance, extremely high nominal load relative to the size of the distribution transformer, incorrect load or transformer phasing, or incorrect load and transformer winding connection type (delta/wye).
High load voltages are usually an indication of incorrect regulation parameters assigned to the regulators or LTCs. These parameters include the voltage target, voltage bandwidth, PT ratio, CT ratio (for devices with line drop compensation), line drop compensation resistance or reactance, or an incorrect regulation unit flag. It may also point to an issue with incorrect nominal or transformer rated voltages.
Message.Solution: Check that the high voltage limit and low voltage limit are reasonable, or that Nodal voltage is reasonable.

Message.MessageText: The nodal voltage is extremely low (<10% nominal) - there may be problems with the model.
Message.Explanation: The load voltage should be at least 10% or there are possible topology errors.

Message.MessageText: Branch flow is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: Flow limit violations may be the result of a circuit that is too heavily loaded (the Converter parameters for setting the loading conditions may not be reasonable). The violations may also be caused by an incorrect conductor size (based on the assigned conductor model). A common case is to have a very small conductor connected between two larger conductors near the head of a feeder. This will likely result in flow violations and excessive voltage drops that will then result in many low voltage violations. The flow violations may also be caused by incorrect limits set on the branch model. The branch (two terminal) device flow limits are given in the switch model, series reactor model, transformer model, and conductor model defined in the global.csv or global_internals.xml file.
Message.Solution: Check that flow limits are reasonable or that Branch flow is reasonable.

Message.MessageText: Distribution transformer flow is outside of its acceptable range.
Message.Explanation: Distribution transformer flow violated flow limit on phase A, or B or C.
Message.Solution: Check that flow limits are reasonable or that Distribution transformer flow is reasonable.

Message.MessageText: Incorrect phasing information given for the primary winding - phasing does not match the assigned transformer type.
Message.Explanation: There are several possible primary winding errors: 1) If the winding is wye connected for single phase transformers, only primary phasing AN, BN, or CN is valid. Otherwise, an error is issued. 2) The winding type is not assigned. 3) If the transformer is a three-phase wye/delta transformer, only primary phasing ABCN is valid. Otherwise, an error is issued. 4) If the transformer is a YDD three winding transformer, only primary phasing AN, BN, or CN is valid. Otherwise, an error is issued. 5) If the transformer is a three-phase delta/delta transformer, only primary phasing ABC is valid. Otherwise, an error is issued. 6) If the transformer is a three-phase delta/wye transformer, only primary phasing ABC is valid. Otherwise, an error is issued. 7) If the transformer is a single-phase regulator, a single-phase wye/wye transformer, or a single-phase auto-transformer, more than one primary phase was specified. It is an error. If Phase A/B/C primary winding is true, the primary phasing must be AN/BN/CN. Otherwise, an error is issued. 8) If the transformer is a single-phase delta/delta transformer, transformer primary should not have the Neutral set and only two phase should be true. Otherwise, an error is issued. 9) If the transformer is a single-phase wye/delta transformer, transformer primary should have the Neutral set and only one phase should be true. Otherwise, an error is issued. 10) If the transformer is a single-phase delta/wye transformer, only two phases should be true and the Primary side should not have the Neutral set. Otherwise, an error is issued. 11) If the transformer has primary wye connection, it will require a neutral (N) phase.
Message.Solution: Find the primary winding errors. The primary phase connections must be consistent with the transformer configuration specified in the TFTYPE_TFMOD field (global.csv file) or parameters specified in the Substation Editor (typically for power transformers).

Message.MessageText: Incorrect phasing information given for the secondary winding - phasing does not match the assigned transformer type.
Message.Explanation: There are several possible secondary winding errors: 1) If the winding is wye connected, only secondary phasing AN, BN, or CN is valid. Otherwise, an error is issued. 2) If the winding is delta connected, check if another transformer in the bank has already been processed. If yes, the AN, BN, or CN phasings are valid. ABC and ABCN phasing is never correct. Otherwise, an error is issued. 3) The winding type is not assigned. 4) If the transformer is a three-phase wye/delta transformer, only secondary phasing ABC is valid. Otherwise, an error is issued. 5) If The transformer is a YDD three winding transformer, only secondary phasing AB or BC or CA is valid. Otherwise, an error is issued. 6) If the transformer is a three-phase delta/delta transformer, only secondary phasing ABC is valid. Otherwise, an error is issued. 7) If the transformer is a three-phase delta/wye transformer, only secondary phasing ABCN is valid. Otherwise, an error is issued. 8) If the transformer is a single-phase regulator, a single-phase wye/wye transformer, or a single-phase auto-transformer, only one secondary phase should be specified, And if Phase A/B/C primary winding is true, the secondary phasing must be AN/BN/CN. Otherwise, an error is issued. 9) If the transformer is a single-phase delta/delta transformer, Transformer secondary should not have the Neutral set and only two phase should be true. Otherwise, an error is issued. 10) If the transformer is a single-phase wye/delta transformer, Transformer secondary should not have the Neutral set and Exactly two phases should exist. Otherwise, an error is issued. 11) If the transformer is a single-phase delta/wye transformer, only one secondary phase should be specified and Secondary side should have the Neutral set. Otherwise, an error is issued.
Message.Solution: Find out the secondary winding errors. Basically, the secondary phase connections must be consistent with the transformer configuration specified in the TFTYPE_TFMOD field (global.csv file) or parameters specified in the Substation Editor (typically for power transformers).

Message.MessageText: Incorrect phasing information given for the tertiary winding - phasing does not match the assigned transformer type.
Message.Explanation: There are several possible tertiary winding errors: 1) If the winding is wye connected, only primary phasing AN, BN, or CN is valid. Otherwise, an error is issued. 2) If the transformer is a three-winding wye/wye/wye transformer, only tertiary phasing ABCN is valid. Otherwise, an error is issued.
Message.Solution: Determine the tertiary winding errors. The tertiary phase connections must be consistent with the transformer configuration specified in the TFTYPE_TFMOD field (global.csv file) or parameters specified in the Substation Editor (typically for power transformers).

Message.MessageText: There are more measurement islands than feeders.
The BLA did not converge - real power load balancing for at least one measurement island was not successful.
Message.Explanation: In Converter, it will set feeder head manual entries as injection, such as, associated feeder breaker phase trip current or feeder peak flow values. If not provided, some default values will be used. This will allow BLA to be executed within DPF. The values need to be reviewed to meet the convergence during the load allocation process. The BLA is diverged because active power mismatch cannot meet the real power convergence tolerance, which is defined in the DNAF_PARAMS.csv file (refer to the ADMS DNAF Analyst Guide for details).
Message.Solution: Review the PeakflowA, PeakflowB, and PeakflowC fields of the Feeder object in the XML/CSV files for feeder injections. Check steps: 1) Open the DPF results file, which has the name “DPF Results_StationName.dat” in the Converter output folder. Search "MEASUREMENT ISLAND CONVERGENCE DETAILS". Find which feeders are real diverged or reactive diverged and the corresponding Real/Reactive Power Mismatches. 2) Review the information message DPF160 in the converter error log. Check the Feeder's manual entry (Amps per phase). 3) Load the model file into the study model file directory. Run DPF in study mode. 4) Bring up the "BLA Feeder Summary" display. Check the calculated flow phase A/B/C (Amps)(kW)(kVAR). It is possible to find the problems and correct PeakflowA, PeakflowB, and PeakflowC of the Feeder.

Message.MessageText: The capacitor regulation branch flow direction was changed to make it consistent with the topology.
Message.Explanation: There are four possible combinations of branch end and flow directions: 1) The upstream node for the regulation branch is the "From" node: a) The capacitor connection node is the same as the upstream node of the regulation branch. The flow is expected to be into the branch at the From end. If not, issue a warning message and change the value of the branch direction (DPF191). Issue a warning message and change the value of the branch end (DPF192). b) The capacitor connection node is the same as the downstream node of the regulation branch. The flow is expected to be out of the branch at the To end. If not, issue a warning message and change the value of the branch direction (DPF191). Issue a warning message and change the value of the branch end (DPF192). 2) The upstream node for the regulation branch is the "To" node: a) The capacitor connection node is the same as the upstream node of the regulation branch. The flow is expected to be out of the branch at the From end. If not, issue a warning message and change the value of the branch direction (DPF191). Issue a warning message and change the value of the branch end (DPF192). b) The capacitor connection node is the same as the downstream node of the regulation branch: The flow is expected to be into the branch at the To end. If not, Issue a warning message and change the value of the branch direction (DPF191). Issue a warning message and change the value of the branch end (DPF192).
Message.Solution: Check if the regulation branch direction and end make sense.

Message.MessageText: The capacitor regulation branch end was changed to make it consistent with the topology.
Message.Explanation: There are four possible combinations of branch end and flow directions: 1) The upstream node for the regulation branch is the "From" node: a) The capacitor connection node is the same as the upstream node of the regulation branch. The flow is expected to be into the branch at the From end. If not, issue a warning message and change the value of the branch direction (DPF191). Issue a warning message and change the value of the branch end (DPF192). b) The capacitor connection node is the same as the downstream node of the regulation branch. The flow is expected to be out of the branch at the To end. If not, issue a warning message and change the value of the branch direction (DPF191). Issue a warning message and change the value of the branch end (DPF192). 2) The upstream node for the regulation branch is the "To" node: a) The capacitor connection node is the same as the upstream node of the regulation branch. The flow is expected to be out of the branch at the From end. If not, issue a warning message and change the value of the branch direction (DPF191). Issue a warning message and change the value of the branch end (DPF192). b) The capacitor connection node is the same as the downstream node of the regulation branch. The flow is expected to be into the branch at the To end. If not, issue a warning message and change the value of the branch direction (DPF191). Issue a warning message and change the value of the branch end (DPF192).
Message.Solution: Check if the regulation branch direction and end make sense.

Message.MessageText: Conflicting grounding information given for a delta secondary winding - the transformer type has a ground but the transformer is ungrounded.
Message.Explanation:
The winding is grounded in the transformer type, not in the transformer instance. There are two possible errors: 1) Find all single-phase transformers in the transformer bank with a split secondary winding (delta connected); the DeltaSecGnd field must be set for only one single-phase transformer. Otherwise, issue errors for every single-phase transformer in the bank. 2) For a three-phase transformer whose secondary winding connection is delta and with one grounded secondary center tap winding, the secondary grounded flag should be true. Otherwise, issue errors.
Check the ground field of the transformer object (Ground = 2,4,6,7) or the DeltaSecGnd field if the transformer is in a transformer bank.
Message.Solution: Check steps: 1) Find the transformer model that a transformer is assigned to. 2) Check the ground information of this tf model. 3) Examine the ground and DeltaSecGnd of the transformer. 4) Check the ground consistency of the tf model and transformer.

Message.MessageText: Conflicting grounding information given for a delta secondary winding - the transformer type does not have a ground but the transformer is grounded.
Message.Explanation:
The winding is not grounded in the transformer type, but is grounded in the transformer instance. There are two possible errors: 1) For a single-phase non-split winding for a delta/delta bank or a wye/delta bank, the DeltaSecGnd field should not be set for every single-phase transformer in the bank. Otherwise, issues an error. 2) For a three-phase transformer with a delta secondary winding or a single-phase wye/delta transformer with non-split winding, the secondary winding should not be grounded.
Check the Ground field of the transformer object, or the DeltaSecGnd field if the transformer is in a transformer bank.
Message.Solution: Check steps: 1) Find the transformer model that a transformer is assigned to. 2) Check the ground information of this tf model. 3) Examine the ground and DeltaSecGnd of the transformer. 4) Check the ground consistency of the tf model and transformer.
